newsitem.title: USA: Former U.S. Fed chief fears rising oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. Fed chief fears rising oil prices.

text.p: Former New York Federal Reserve Bank president Gerald Corrigan expressed concern on Thursday at the prospect of rising oil prices amid growing tensions in the Middle East.

Corrigan, now an international adviser at Goldman Sachs, said he was most worried about the political situation in Saudi Arabia, a country experiencing what he termed "a surprisingly strong wave of anti-U.S. sentiment".
Also of concern were ongoing tensions encompassing Iraq, Iran and the stalled Israeli-PLO peace process, he said.

"When I think about all these things taken together, I end up saying to myself, well what about oil? And I say to myself, what about U.S. energy policy? And, of course, what I quickly conclude is, we ain't got one," he told a business dinner hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.

"And we are far more vulnerable to Middle Eastern oil today than we were in 1973 or 1979. We have no policy. And I would also note, I don't hear a lot of talk about energy policy in the political campaign," Corrigan said.
